rv.q: The musical makes Charlie seem less of a drip than he was in the movie.
Director/choreographer Jerry Mitchell marshals it all with smooth efficiency, and drives it with sexy, sassy class.
With its infectious energy and richly enjoyable performances, Kinky Boots feels like a show that has got legs.
And yet the whole thing canters along with engaging verve and vim, once a dull opening 15 minutes first quarter is done.
It's good fun but, in my view, a bit too formulaic to induce rapture.
He’s a sure-footed sensation, the clod-hopping show isn’t.
In summary, this show really doesn’t put a single stilettoed foot wrong.

And, in this glorious feel-good musical by Harvey Fierstein (book) and Cyndi Lauper (music and lyrics), those boots are made for walking, talking, singing, flouncing and wearing well above the kneecap.

cn.t: This big-hearted Broadway import wins over critics with its high-energy choreography and feelgood spirit, though one reviewer finds it formulaic. Most praise the show's glorious physicality and charm despite its predictable factory-to-fabulous premise.
